main_text.p: ptione in primo congressu magnam sanguinis profusionem manare volunt.
Hystera seu fundus uteri est pars ejus supra cervicè, membranosum receptaculum, & humanæ formationis officina, involvendo fœtui accommodata.Vteri fundus.
Superficies fundi uterini est cum Exterior, tum Interior.
Exterior est vitulinæ fronti, cornua jam producenti, non absimilis, duos obtusos angulos instar cornuum, in qua vasa semen deferentia inseruntur, profe-rens.
Interior est aspera, plurimis porositatibus conspicuis prædita, & quidem sinus simplex, non multis cellulis direm-tus.

Fundi uteri os seu orificium est rimula semper connivens, nisi naturali instinctu vel semen admittat, vel fœtui mensibusq; iter præbeat. Hic, egrediente fœtu, sedes acutissimi est doloris, mulierum in partu.
main_text.head: CAPUT XXXIX. DE FIBRIS.

page.notes: Marginal notes at the right beside the lines near "Superficies" and "Interior" and at the foot of the column are faint and only partly legible; they are left out. The note "Vteri fundus." is the only one read with confidence. The word "semen" in the Exterior paragraph is read from a slightly blurred scan. The catchword "Hacte-" is read as printed. The 'profe-rens' and 'direm-tus' line-end hyphens are kept as printed. The page has show-through from the reverse side, which is not transcribed.
